Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

bah! interjection

contempt, impatience

also pooh, pooh-pooh, pah, pshaw, tush, tut-tut, tut tut, tsk

classical

Ter. Haut. 587: Vah! quasi dēsit locus.
Plaut. Amph. 579b–580: Vah, apage tē ā mē.

Vah!

bah! pah!

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Lewis & Short: astonishment, joy, anger; with apage or a scornful remark it is contempt.

Other words

  • Phy! — pish! tush!

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 412b

    (vōx cōmica: once in Ter.)

    Lewis & Short: “pish! tush!”; Syrus pooh-poohing Demea’s pride in his son.

  • Apage! — away with it! nonsense!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 310: Apage, nōn placet mē hoc noctis ēsse

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: never in Cicero))

    See also go away and yucky.

  • Ō tempora, ō mōrēs! — what times! what manners! (tut-tut)

    also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.2

    (Cicero’s oratory, quoted in jest)

    The stock lament over the way things are going; said of small scandals it is the Latinist’s “tut-tut”.

Examples

  • Abī deambulātum. — Deambulātum quō? — Vah! quasi dēsit locus.

    Go for a walk. — A walk where? — Pah! as if there were nowhere to go.Ter. Haut. 587

  • Vah, apage tē ā mē.

    Bah, get away from me.Plaut. Amph. 579b–580

  • Syre, praeceptōrum plēnus istōrum ille. — Phy. — Domī habuit unde disceret.

    He’s full of those precepts, Syrus. — Pooh! — He had someone at home to learn from.Ter. Ad. 412–413

  • Ō tempora, ō mōrēs!

    What times! What ways!Cic. Cat. 1.2

See also nonsense!, yucky, go, ah!.
